results.name: outlier_example_neighborhood
results.description: For sets of >=3 examples where exactly one example breaks the majority last digit, yes rate among non-example targets within 3 of that outlier that do not end in the majority digit; observed below null means humans discount the exceptional example (do not generalise around it) more than the model, which places it inside a covering interval, above null means they treat it as a genuine member more.
results.code:
# name: outlier_example_neighborhood
# description: For sets of >=3 examples where exactly one example breaks the majority last digit, yes rate among non-example targets within 3 of that outlier that do not end in the majority digit; observed below null means humans discount the exceptional example (do not generalise around it) more than the model, which places it inside a covering interval, above null means they treat it as a genuine member more.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    dist = np.where(valid, np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), np.inf)
    nearest = dist.min(axis=1)
    nonmember = nearest > 0
    lo = np.where(valid, ex, np.inf).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, ex, -np.inf).max(axis=1)
    ld = np.where(valid, np.mod(ex, 10), np.nan)
    cnt = np.stack([(ld == d).sum(axis=1) for d in range(10)], axis=1)
    maj = cnt.argmax(axis=1); majc = cnt.max(axis=1)
    is_out = valid & (ld != maj[:, None])
    dout = np.where(is_out, np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), np.inf).min(axis=1)
    m = (n >= 3) & (majc == n - 1) & nonmember & (dout <= 3) & (np.mod(t, 10) != maj)
    return float(r[m].mean()) if m.any() else 0.0

results.name: any_shared_digit_far
results.description: Among non-example targets more than 5 from the nearest example, yes rate for targets sharing any digit (ones or tens) with at least one example minus targets sharing none; observed above null means people use digit-level similarity to individual examples more than the model's whole-rule/interval hypotheses predict, below null means less.
results.code:
# name: any_shared_digit_far
# description: Among non-example targets more than 5 from the nearest example, yes rate for targets sharing any digit (ones or tens) with at least one example minus targets sharing none; observed above null means people use digit-level similarity to individual examples more than the model's whole-rule/interval hypotheses predict, below null means less.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    dist = np.where(valid, np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), np.inf)
    nearest = dist.min(axis=1)
    nonmember = nearest > 0
    lo = np.where(valid, ex, np.inf).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, ex, -np.inf).max(axis=1)
    def digs(x):
        x = np.nan_to_num(x, nan=-1)
        return [np.where(x >= 0, np.mod(x, 10), -1), np.where(x >= 10, np.mod(np.floor(x / 10), 10), -2), np.where(x >= 100, 1, -3)]
    E = digs(ex); T = digs(t[:, None])
    share = np.zeros(len(t), dtype=bool)
    for a_ in E:
        for b_ in T:
            share |= ((a_ == b_) & (a_ >= 0) & valid).any(axis=1)
    m = nonmember & (nearest > 5)
    a = r[m & share]; b = r[m & ~share]
    if len(a) == 0 or len(b) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(a.mean() - b.mean())

results.name: near_gradient_1_vs_2to5
results.description: Among non-example targets, yes rate at distance exactly 1 from the nearest example minus yes rate at distance 2-5; observed below null means humans accept immediate neighbours (which change last digit/parity) less than the interval model predicts, above null means a steeper proximity peak than the model.

results.name: above_vs_below_near
results.description: Among non-example targets 1-10 from the nearest example and outside the examples' range, yes rate for targets above the max example minus targets below the min example; observed above null means people still extend upward more than the compressed-number-line model predicts, below null means the model now over-produces upward extension.

results.name: cell_unanimity
results.description: Fraction of (set, target) cells with >=2 responses in which all responses agree; observed above null means responses are more deterministic/extreme per item than the model's graded posterior predicts, below null means more disagreement.
results.code:
# name: cell_unanimity
# description: Fraction of (set, target) cells with >=2 responses in which all responses agree; observed above null means responses are more deterministic/extreme per item than the model's graded posterior predicts, below null means more disagreement.
def test_statistic(df):
    ex = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(int).to_numpy().astype(float)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    valid = ~np.isnan(ex)
    n = valid.sum(axis=1)
    dist = np.where(valid, np.abs(ex - t[:, None]), np.inf)
    nearest = dist.min(axis=1)
    nonmember = nearest > 0
    lo = np.where(valid, ex, np.inf).min(axis=1)
    hi = np.where(valid, ex, -np.inf).max(axis=1)
    key = df["number_set"].astype(str) + "|" + df["target"].astype(str)
    g = pd.DataFrame({"k": key.to_numpy(), "r": r}).groupby("k")["r"].agg(["mean", "count"])
    g = g[g["count"] >= 2]
    if len(g) == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(((g["mean"] == 0) | (g["mean"] == 1)).mean())
